problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{3},\,{t}^{2}⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$

feedback.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{-2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩\cdot ⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩ \\  & ={e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{({e}^{t})}^{2}+{(2{e}^{-2t})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
